english.title: Manufacturer of electrical equipment fail to comply with procedures for series production
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a manufacturer of electrical equipment namely **(..SPECIFY EQUIPMENT..), which was manufactured by series production, failed to ensure that the equipment is in conformity with Part 2 of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016, **(..SPECIFY NON-COMPLIANCE WITH PRINCIPAL ELEMENTS OF SAFETY OBJECTIVES OR OBLIGATIONS IN SECTIONS 4 - 35..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 10, 50(1) and 51(1) of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
manufacturer of electrical equipment manufactured by series production
failed to ensure conformity with Part 2 of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) 'Conformity with Part 2' is defined in regulation 2 of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.
(ii) In ensuring that procedures are in place, the manufacturer must take adequate account of changes in design, characteristics, a harmonised standard or other technical specification, see regulation 10(2) of the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
